note: independent recomputation from raw TSVs; calibration constant fitted on narrow sub-bands and extrapolated, to remove the fit-and-test-on-the-same-band circularity

registration.map: response row i -> grid index i for i<=66; i+1 for i>=67

statistic: rel_dev = 1 - (L_k/F(T,M_k))/c_hat ;  |.| pooled over 5 levels x band points

quantization_floor.note: photon_flux_cm2 in the grid carries only 3 significant figures; the half-step of that rounding, relative to the value, is the smallest honest residual scale

cross_band_c_stability_5800K.note: a genuine global proportionality forces c_hat to be the same on every band; the relative spread of c_hat across bands IS the extrapolation error

extrapolation_penalty.note: out-of-band residual exceeds in-band residual by this factor; both sit at the 3-significant-figure rounding floor of the flux grid

verdict.conclusion: Genuine global proportionality, NOT a band-local fit. Extrapolating a constant fitted only on 500-700 nm, or only on 400-500 nm, or only on 750-850 nm, reproduces the 330-500 nm and 700-850 nm bands to mean |dev| ~1.1e-3 and max |dev| <= 4.3e-3, i.e. the same magnitude as inside the fitting window (mean ~1.0e-3, max <= 2.2e-3). The residual is not merely small, it is entirely accounted for by the 3-significant-figure rounding of photon_flux_cm2 in the grid: 98.5% of points fall inside their own rounding half-step, and the mean |dev| (1.085e-3) matches the uniform-rounding expectation (1.059e-3). A wrong temperature slice degrades mean |dev| to 0.093-0.151 and max |dev| to 0.50-1.05, two orders of magnitude worse, so the statistic does have discriminating power. Limitation: the flux axis carries only 3 significant figures, so no test on this data can resolve deviations below ~0.2-0.5%, and any claim of accuracy finer than that is unfalsifiable here. Prior 'sub-1%' claims are therefore (a) not circular, and (b) at the noise floor, but they cannot be pushed to the 0.01% level with this file.
